scope.edition: English Repos base game, 2021 publication; sc-en01 rulebook © 2020
scope.included: Complete standard setup, Choosing Clues, Resolution, verification geometry and orientation, scoring, cleanup and end of game.

checked_claims.claim: Cooperative word-association game, collective high-score objective, 220 Keyword cards, six boards, six markers, Record of Legends and rulebook.
source_refs: PDF p. 1, opening overview and CONTENTS; p. 6, END OF THE GAME

checked_claims.claim: Each player receives a board and marker; deck is shuffled and face down within reach; four cards are drawn and randomly placed in the recessed spaces, hidden from others.
Choosing Clues is simultaneous and individual; Resolution is collaborative. Each player is Spectator once; first Spectator is chosen at Resolution and later Spectators proceed to the left.
source_refs: PDF p. 2, GAMEPLAY and 1. CHOOSING CLUES, first paragraph; p. 4, 2. RESOLUTION, first paragraph; p. 5, final paragraph

checked_claims.claim: Eight outside-edge Keywords form four Pairs, with two Keywords below each Clue Zone; each of four Clues connects both Keywords and goes in the corresponding zone.
source_refs: PDF p. 2, 1. CHOOSING CLUES, text and labeled board diagram

checked_claims.claim: One word per Clue; compounds permitted; listed noun, proper noun, acronym, number and onomatopoeia categories and examples accurately reproduced.
source_refs: PDF p. 2, 1. CHOOSING CLUES, final paragraphs

checked_claims.claim: Either Keyword, translations, same-family words and made-up words are prohibited; the summary accurately reproduces the Amour, Prince and Cuppajo examples.
source_refs: PDF p. 3, Invalid Clues, all three bullets and examples

checked_claims.claim: Advice to use the first word that comes to mind is included as advice without displacing the clue restrictions.
source_refs: PDF p. 3, ADVICE, read together with Invalid Clues

checked_claims.claim: After four Clues, remove all four cards; draw one unseen new card; shuffle all five; pile them face down on the board in front of the owner; wait until all players finish before Resolution.
Spectator cannot communicate in any way during their Resolution and places their board plus all five cards face up in the table center.
source_refs: PDF p. 4, 2. RESOLUTION, first and second paragraphs

checked_claims.claim: Other players use Clues to reconstruct the original Pairs in the board spaces; cards may be placed while discussing; the player left of the Spectator decides disagreements; verification follows agreed placement.
source_refs: PDF p. 4, 2. RESOLUTION, second paragraph, disagreement paragraph, ADVICE and final paragraph

checked_claims.claim: Correctness requires card space and orientation. The verification drawing marks the lower-left card incorrect while marking three other cards correct, supporting removal and scoring by card rather than by individual Pair.
source_refs: PDF p. 2, labeled Pair geometry diagram; p. 5, VERIFICATION diagram, red rotation arrow and lower-left red cross; p. 5, First attempt / Error and Second attempt

checked_claims.claim: All correct on first attempt scores one point per card plus two bonus points, six total, with the board then finished.
source_refs: PDF p. 5, VERIFICATION / First attempt / Perfect; subsequent Error branch expressly supplies the second attempt

checked_claims.claim: Any incorrect Pair triggers silent removal of incorrect cards to the table center and a second and final attempt. The summary allows only prescribed feedback and gives no unauthorized hinting.
source_refs: PDF p. 4, 2. RESOLUTION, Spectator communication prohibition; p. 5, VERIFICATION / First attempt / Error

checked_claims.claim: After agreed second placement, remove incorrect cards to table center; score one point per correct card, zero to four, with no bonus and no third attempt.
source_refs: PDF p. 5, VERIFICATION / First attempt / Error, final sentence; Second attempt, full paragraph

checked_claims.claim: After resolution, turn the board over, write its points in the middle, discard all five used cards, and pass Spectator role left.
After every player has been Spectator once, end the game, add all board scores, enter team score in Record of Legends, and compare against prior high score.
source_refs: PDF p. 6, END OF THE GAME, all paragraphs

checked_claims.claim: Designer and copyright match the rulebook. Player count and play time are not stated in its six pages. Optional Add a Challenge is explicitly excluded consistently with the requested scope.
source_refs: PDF p. 1, designer credit; p. 6, CREDITS and copyright; PDF pp. 1–6, absence of player-count/play-time specifications; p. 6, ADD A CHALLENGE
